title: SpaceX Stock (SPCX) Rises 0.7% to $143.09 (Nov 10)
summary: SpaceX (SPCX) rose 0.72% to $143.09 on Nov 10 as the Nasdaq fell 0.74%, on the day Singulus announced a solar cell line contract with SpaceX.
body_markdown:
The close leaves SpaceX stock 36.58% below its 52-week high of $225.64 and 36.50% above its 52-week low of $104.83. According to[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spcx-secures-singulus-deal-scale-205809395.html) , the shares also remain above the $135 price of SpaceX's June[initial public offering](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) .


## Why SpaceX Stock Rose


None of the reports reviewed for this article named a company-specific cause for the gain, which came as the Nasdaq fell. Three pieces of SpaceX news were reported on Tuesday.


As reported by[Stocktwits](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spcx-secures-singulus-deal-scale-205809395.html) , German equipment maker Singulus Technologies announced on Tuesday a supply contract with SpaceX for a turnkey production line for heterojunction solar cells, built for the planned Starmind satellite constellation at SpaceX's Bastrop, Texas facility. According to Singulus, the initial order is worth more than €60 million (about $67 million), and the first line is scheduled for delivery in the first half of 2027.


Per[Benzinga](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/spacex-could-profit-ai-data-210007229.html) , Deutsche Bank analyst Edison Yu raised his 2028 revenue estimate for SpaceX by $18.7 billion to $315.3 billion, reflecting a larger contribution from the company's cloud business. The bank expects cloud computing to account for more than half of SpaceX's fourth-quarter revenue.


According to[TheStreet](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/googles-spacex-investment-takes-unexpected-201300786.html) , citing a holdings update reported by Reuters, Alphabet's SpaceX position rose to about 555 million shares from 551.2 million. The report also said longtime Google executive Don Harrison left SpaceX's board, which SpaceX said did not stem from any disagreement over operations or policies.


## SPCX Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Google agreed to pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity from October 2026 through June 2029, according to TheStreet, citing a filing tied to SpaceX's IPO as reported by Reuters.
- Deutsche Bank expects political pressure to slow data center construction, mainly in 2028, keeping compute scarce and rental prices higher, Benzinga reported.
- SpaceX has filed with the FCC for authority to operate up to one million Starmind satellites, with first launches expected in the latter half of 2027, per Stocktwits.


### Risks


- Either Google or SpaceX can exit the computing contract with 90 days' notice once 2026 ends, according to TheStreet.
- Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to halt new data center approvals until lawmakers set protections, which Benzinga said could expose SpaceX's planned $24 billion gas-fired power and computing project in Texas.
- Elon Musk wrote on X on Monday that "if compute becomes plentiful and cheap, SpaceX revenue will drop," Benzinga reported.
